_notes: Page 52 heading numeral is visually ambiguous between סימן לה (35) and סימן לח (38) -- multiple careful zoomed crops looked like a closed ח (gate shape, no visible gap), but that reading would break strict sequential ordering (would need to jump 34->38, then backward to לו=36 later on the same page, then לז=37 on page 53, which is inconsistent). Resolved as siman 35 per the strict-sequential rule (34 on p46-51, then 35 on p52 right column, 36 on p52 left column [very short filler teshuva], 37 on p53). If this proves wrong, re-check page 52 top-right heading closely -- possible ink bleed closing the gap in ה making it look like ח.

Page 123's siman heading was initially misread as siman 108 (קח) -- a very careful high-zoom letter check seemed to show the second letter's two legs fully closed/connected (favoring chet over heh), but this produced an impossible ordering: page 124's left column clearly contains simanim 106 (קו, lulav taken by a woman without permission) then 107 (קז, lulav taken by a minor) in that order, which can only be sequentially consistent if the long selichot/chatzot essay heading on page 123 (continuing through page 124's right column, ending right before 106) is siman 105 (קה), not 108. Corrected to 105. This is exactly the ר/ד, ה/ח-style ambiguity already flagged elsewhere in this volume -- trust the running count and cross-page ordering over the individual zoomed-letter read when they conflict. If siman 108 is later found to be missing/duplicated further on, re-check this page 123 heading again.

Volume ends at siman 113, which spans pages 130-132 (the last page of the volume). Page 132 ends with the signature 'משה פיינשטיין' followed by a printer's decorative end-of-volume ornament and no further text -- confirming there is NO back matter/index in this volume (same pattern as sibling volume IggrotMosheOH3, not IggrotMosheEH3 which had back matter after siman 50). Indexing complete: simanim 1-113, pages 3-132.
